name: Hard cut (straight cut)
definition: Shot A ends and shot B begins on the next frame. The default join in narrative film; implies continuous time unless other cues say otherwise.
how: Cut where the next shot answers a question the viewer has (who is speaking, what is she looking at). Name the attention cue before the cut.
how_html: rig.js: R.cut(t). Plain HTML/GSAP: tl.set('#shotA',{autoAlpha:0},t); tl.set('#shotB',{autoAlpha:1},t);
how_ffmpeg: ffmpeg -i a.mp4 -i b.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v][0:a][1:v][1:a]concat=n=2:v=1:a=1[v][a]" -map "[v]" -map "[a]" out.mp4  (or concat demuxer with a list file when codecs match)
how_hyperframes: Two clips on the same track, B's data-start = A's data-start + A's data-duration. Note: HyperFrames' animation guide says 'every composition uses transitions' for motion graphics; for narrative scenes a hard cut IS the correct transition - document the choice.
purpose: Move attention to new information with no felt delay.
use_when: the next shot is cued by a look, sound, or motion
avoid_when: two shots of the same subject with tiny size/angle change (reads as a jump cut)
no attention cue and a big change of screen position of the subject
breaks_continuity_when: subject jumps to the opposite side of frame, screen direction flips, or framing changes less than ~30 degrees / one shot size (jump). Smith2012: unmet expectations force effortful a-posteriori reconstruction.

examples.note: match-action cut puts Rachael's face where Deckard's had been, so attention transfers smoothly

ai_image_prompt: Generate A and B as separate frames; B: keep the subject's face in the same screen third as in A (e.g. 'subject's face in the right third of frame').
ai_video_prompt: Generate each shot separately; end shot A on a motion or a look so the cut has a cue.
common_mistakes: cutting on a still frame with no cue
cutting before the line/action resolves
check: Play at full speed: does your eye land on the subject within ~3 frames after the cut?

name: Cut on action / match on action
definition: Cut in the middle of a movement (stand, turn, open, throw) and continue the movement from a new angle.
how: Overlap the action: let A run 2-4 frames into the motion, start B a few frames after the matching pose; motion direction on screen stays the same.
how_html: rig.js: animate the puppet turn across t-0.15..t+0.15; R.cut(t) at mid-turn; in shot B start the same tween at its midpoint (gsap tl.fromTo(..., {progress:0.5}) or set rotation to the mid value).
how_ffmpeg: Trim A to end mid-motion (-t), trim B to start at the matching pose (-ss), then concat. Find frames with: ffmpeg -i b.mp4 -vf "select='between(t,1.0,1.5)',showinfo" -f null -
how_hyperframes: Hard cut between clips; set clip B's media start offset so the pose matches; keep motion direction on screen consistent.
purpose: Hide the join; motion carries the eye across the cut.
use_when: joining two AI/2D shots that don't match perfectly
any physical action covered from two angles
avoid_when: you want the cut to be felt (use smash or jump cut)
breaks_continuity_when: motion direction reverses on screen, or the pose in B is clearly earlier/later than in A (double action or missing action).

examples.work: Feature-film excerpts in an edit-detection task
examples.note: about a third of edits coinciding with sudden motion onset went undetected even when viewers were looking for cuts
a woman's turn carries the eye through a cut to a completely different scene

ai_image_prompt: Two frames of the same pose mid-turn from two angles: 'same character, mid head-turn to the left, 3/4 view' and 'same character, mid head-turn to the left, profile view, same costume and light'.
ai_video_prompt: Shot A: 'medium shot, she begins to stand up from the chair'. Shot B: 'wide shot, she is halfway up from the chair and finishes standing' - cut at the halfway pose.
common_mistakes: cutting after the motion ends (loses the cover)
repeating too much of the motion (double action)
check: Scrub the 6 frames around the cut: one continuous motion, same direction.

name: Graphic match cut
definition: Shape, colour, position or motion repeats across a cut joining two different places/times, linking them in meaning.
how: Put the matching shape in the same screen position and size in A and B; cut on the frame where they align.
how_html: Layer A and B in the same container; align the shape centres (same left/top %); R.cut(t). Optionally 4-6 frame dissolve if the alignment is imperfect.
how_ffmpeg: Crop/scale B so the shape aligns: [1:v]scale=...,crop=...[b]; then concat. Optional xfade=transition=fade:duration=0.15 for imperfect matches.
how_hyperframes: Two clips; use hyperframes-keyframes 'visual match handoff' to scale/position B so the shapes coincide at the cut.
purpose: Make a connection (idea, time jump, metaphor) without words.
use_when: a visual metaphor is the story point
avoid_when: the link carries no meaning (it draws attention to the editing for nothing)
breaks_continuity_when: always breaks place/time - that is its job; fails when the shapes are not at the same screen position, so the eye has to search.

examples.note: bone-to-spacecraft cut, discussed in our curriculum 11-edit-grade.md; [CRAFT, unverified example] in this session's sources

ai_image_prompt: Generate B with an init/reference of A's silhouette: 'round lens of the glasses centred in frame, same size and position as the full moon in the previous shot'.
ai_video_prompt: Both shots: 'static camera, circular object centred, slow clockwise rotation' so motion matches too.
common_mistakes: shapes at different positions
matching shape but mismatched motion speed
check: Onion-skin last frame of A over first frame of B at 50%: shapes overlap.

name: J-cut (audio leads)
definition: Sound of shot B starts before its picture appears.
how: Start B's audio 0.3-2 s before the picture cut. Works best with a sound that makes the viewer want to see its source.
how_html: HTML audio/HyperFrames audio element for B starts at t-lead; picture R.cut(t).
how_ffmpeg: Picture: concat a,b. Audio: [1:a]adelay=<(durA-lead)*1000>|<...>[ba]; [0:a]atrim=0:durA-lead,afade=t=out:st=durA-lead-0.1:d=0.1[aa]; [aa][ba]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0 (or acrossfade=d=0.2 for a smooth overlap).
how_hyperframes: Audio clip of B gets data-start earlier than its video clip; use hyperframes-audio crossfade for the overlap.
purpose: Pull the viewer into the next scene; motivate the cut by sound (an AToCC attention cue).
use_when: a character is about to speak off-screen
avoid_when: the sound would spoil a reveal that should be a surprise
breaks_continuity_when: the pre-lapped sound is ambiguous and the viewer attributes it to scene A.

examples.note: attention shifts to the off-screen speaker's last screen location ~200 ms after their speech starts - sound cues the eye before the cut

common_mistakes: lead too long so the viewer is confused
no level change so the incoming sound is inaudible
check: With eyes closed: do you know a new scene is coming? With eyes open: does the cut feel expected?

name: L-cut (audio trails)
definition: Sound of shot A continues over the picture of shot B. Classic use: speaker's line continues while we see the listener react.
how: Cut picture to the reaction mid-line; keep A's dialogue running; let B's ambience fade up under it.
how_html: Keep A's audio element playing past R.cut(t) to t+trail.
how_ffmpeg: Picture concat; audio: [0:a] full length; [1:a]adelay=durA_ms,volume=... ; amix=inputs=2:normalize=0.
how_hyperframes: Extend A's audio clip data-duration beyond its video clip; B's video starts at the cut.
purpose: Show the effect of words on the listener; keep conversation flow.
use_when: big lines - cut to the listener (story-clips GUIDE)
avoid_when: the speaker's face carries the key emotion of the line
breaks_continuity_when: lip movements of the listener contradict the audio (looks like bad sync).
ai_image_prompt: Listener reaction frame: 'close-up, she listens, eyes lowering slightly, lips closed'.
ai_video_prompt: 'close-up of a listener, lips closed, subtle reaction: a slow blink and swallow, no speaking'.
common_mistakes: generated listener moves lips (AI often adds talking)
check: Listener's mouth closed for the whole trailing line.

name: Reaction cut
definition: Cut to a character's face responding to what was said/seen. The reaction tells the audience how to feel (Kuleshov logic).
how: Hold the reaction long enough for one readable change (blink, breath, look-away): 0.8-2 s.
how_html: R.cut(t) to close-up layer; animate one micro-change (eyelid, head tilt) at t+0.3.
how_ffmpeg: Insert clip; concat.
how_hyperframes: Insert clip with data-duration 0.8-2 s; L-cut the dialogue over it.
purpose: Direct the emotional reading of an event.
use_when: after a key line or reveal
to delay a reveal (show the face first)
avoid_when: the face is truly blank - studies show context only nudges ambiguous faces
breaks_continuity_when: eyeline points away from where the source is on screen.

examples.note: context shifts emotion reading of a neutral face; fearful contexts strongest, happy contexts weak or null

ai_image_prompt: 'close-up, character looking screen-left toward the off-screen event, eyes widening slightly, soft key light from screen-left'.
ai_video_prompt: 'close-up, static camera, the character reacts: eyes widen slightly, breath held, then a slow blink; no head movement'.
common_mistakes: reaction with no change
eyeline in wrong direction
check: Mute and watch: is the emotion readable from the reaction alone?

name: Eyeline match / POV cut
definition: A looks off-screen; cut to what A sees (POV) or to the object at the matching direction.
how: A's gaze direction and B's placement agree: A looks screen-right -> object appears from the right side/centre; for POV, match height and lens feel.
how_html: Puppet head/eye rotation toward the cut direction 0.2-0.4 s before R.cut(t).
how_ffmpeg: Concat; time the cut ~6-10 frames after the head turn completes.
how_hyperframes: Hard cut; place B's subject in the screen region the gaze pointed to.
purpose: Tell us what the character attends to; build subjectivity.
use_when: introducing a prop/product through a character's interest
avoid_when: the looked-at object will be shown in the same shot anyway
breaks_continuity_when: gaze direction and target position disagree - viewer saccades the wrong way (Smith2012 owl example).

examples.note: gaze cues link characters never shown in the same space; a mismatched gaze shift sends attention the wrong way

ai_image_prompt: A: 'medium close-up, she looks off-screen right and slightly down'. B (POV): 'high angle POV looking down at a pair of glasses on a wooden counter'.
ai_video_prompt: A: 'she turns her head to look off-screen right, eyes focus'. B: 'POV, slight handheld drift, looking down at the counter'.
common_mistakes: POV height wrong (adult POV at child height)
AI regenerates the looker in the POV shot
check: Draw an arrow from A's eyes - does B's subject sit at the arrow's end?

name: Axial cut / punch-in
definition: Cut straight along the lens axis to a closer (or wider) framing of the same subject.
how: Change at least one, preferably two, shot sizes (MS->CU) so it reads as intentional, not a jump cut. Common in vertical video as a 'digital punch-in' on a beat.
how_html: Same layer, set transform scale 1 -> 1.6 at t with transformOrigin on the face (instant set, not tween).
how_ffmpeg: [0:v]trim=start=2:end=4,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,crop=iw/1.6:ih/1.6:x:y,scale=1080:1920[b] then concat with the wide part.
how_hyperframes: hyperframes-keyframes punch-in: tl.set(clip,{scale:1.6,transformOrigin:'50% 35%'},t).
purpose: Emphasis: the face/detail just became important.
use_when: product detail punch-ins (house rule for glasses clips)
avoid_when: scale change < ~1.3x (reads as an error)
upscaled source becomes soft
breaks_continuity_when: size change is too small (jump-cut feel) or the subject moves position between A and B.
ai_image_prompt: Generate the CU at native resolution instead of cropping: 'extreme close-up of the hinge of the glasses, same lighting as the wide shot'.
common_mistakes: soft upscaled crops
punch-in on every beat (loses meaning)
check: Size ratio >= 1.3; face/detail stays at the same screen point.

name: Insert
definition: A close shot of a detail within the scene (hand, label, screen, price tag) cut into the coverage.
how: Insert is 0.7-2 s; match light direction and the hand/object position from the master.
how_html: Overlay layer with the detail image, R.cut in and out.
how_ffmpeg: Split the master and concat [master_part1][insert][master_part2]; keep master audio continuous under the insert (overlay audio from master).
how_hyperframes: Insert clip on a higher track over the master's time range; master audio continues.
purpose: Deliver information the wide shot cannot show.
avoid_when: the detail does not matter to the story
breaks_continuity_when: object state differs from master (glass full vs empty) near the attention point.
ai_image_prompt: 'macro insert shot of a finger touching the nose pad of the glasses, same warm key light from the left as the master shot'.
ai_video_prompt: 'macro, shallow depth of field, finger slowly adjusts the nose pad, static camera'.
common_mistakes: different hand/skin tone than master
light from the opposite side
check: Light direction and hand identity match the master.

name: Cutaway
definition: Cut to something outside the main action (another place, an object, a crowd) then back.
how: Keep it short and motivated (sound, look, story); return to the main action at a later point in time to compress time.
how_html: Swap layer for the cutaway, then R.cut back; skip ahead in the main action.
how_ffmpeg: Concat [main_a][cutaway][main_b] where main_b starts later than main_a ended (time compression).
how_hyperframes: Cutaway clip between two segments of the main clip; adjust main clip media offset.
purpose: Compress time, hide a bad section, give context, comic aside.
emotional_effect: irony (cut to something contradicting the dialogue)
use_when: a joke or comment on the action
avoid_when: it breaks a held emotional moment
breaks_continuity_when: the cutaway has no link to the scene - viewer asks 'where is this?'.
ai_image_prompt: 'wall clock in the shop, same warm afternoon light'.
ai_video_prompt: 'static shot of the shop clock, second hand moving'.
common_mistakes: random B-roll unrelated to the beat
check: Can you state why we are here in one phrase?

name: Cross-cutting / parallel editing
definition: Alternate between two or more lines of action in different places, usually implying simultaneity.
how: Establish each line clearly once; shorten the alternation as the lines converge; keep each line's screen direction consistent (e.g. hero moves L->R, victim's threat R->L).
how_html: Two scene groups; R.cut between them with decreasing intervals (e.g. 3s, 2s, 1.2s, 0.7s).
how_ffmpeg: Split each line into segments and concat alternately; generate the segment list with a script.
how_hyperframes: Alternate clips from two sub-compositions on one track; shorten data-duration progressively.
purpose: Suspense, comparison, irony.
avoid_when: the audience doesn't know the stakes - suspense needs known stakes and odds
continuity_effect: breaks place on purpose; preserves time logic
breaks_continuity_when: the viewer cannot tell which line a shot belongs to (similar locations, no distinguishing colour/light).

examples.note: villains trap the heroine while the distant hero races back - suspense from a likely bad outcome vs unlikely good one (Carroll's theory via Allen)
viewers with prior context perceived the cross-cut 6-shot sequence as more coherent

ai_image_prompt: Give each line a colour signature: line A 'cool blue night light', line B 'warm tungsten interior'.
ai_video_prompt: Line A: 'camera tracking left-to-right with the runner'. Line B: 'static, slow push-in on the waiting woman'.
common_mistakes: equal-length alternation (no build)
lines look alike
check: Show any frame to a fresh viewer: can they name the line?

name: Jump cut
definition: A cut between two shots of the same subject from (nearly) the same position, so the subject appears to jump in time/position.
how: Use deliberately: remove pauses in talking-head, show time passing in one location, or create restlessness. Keep framing identical so the jump is clearly intentional.
how_html: Same background layer; swap the character pose layer at t with no camera change.
how_ffmpeg: Use silence detection to cut talking-head pauses: ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -af silencedetect=n=-35dB:d=0.4 -f null - ; then trim/concat kept segments.
how_hyperframes: talking-head-recut skill does this for speech; otherwise consecutive clips from the same source.
purpose: Compression, energy, unease, vlog style.
avoid_when: you want an invisible continuity edit
breaks_continuity_when: always visible; becomes an error when unintended (two takes of an AI shot with small framing drift).

examples.note: most contain a handful of jump cuts (Salt, via Smith 2012)

ai_image_prompt: Lock framing: same seed/composition, only the pose changes.
common_mistakes: accidental jump between two similar generated shots
check: If unintended: change shot size by >= one step or angle by >= 30 degrees.

name: Smash cut
definition: An abrupt cut from one mood/sound level to a sharply contrasting one (quiet to loud, calm to chaos, line to its contradiction).
how: Cut mid-sentence or at the peak; contrast in sound level and image brightness/scale is what makes it 'smash'.
how_html: R.cut(t) with an audio level jump and a different palette layer.
how_ffmpeg: Concat; ensure B's audio starts at full level (no fade): afade only on A if needed.
how_hyperframes: Hard cut; sound effect hit at the cut frame from the SFX library.
purpose: Shock or comic contradiction ('I'll never do that' -> doing it).
avoid_when: used repeatedly (loses force)
breaks_continuity_when: by design.
ai_image_prompt: A: 'calm pastel bedroom, soft morning light'. B: 'same character, chaotic crowded street, harsh midday light'.
common_mistakes: fading into the smash (kills it)
check: Waveform shows a level step at the cut; brightness histogram changes sharply.

name: Sound bridge / sound match
definition: A sound continues or rhymes across a cut between different scenes (a scream becomes a train whistle; music carries over).
how: Find two sounds with similar pitch/envelope; cross at the picture cut.
how_html: Two audio elements, crossfade 0.1-0.3 s at t.
how_ffmpeg: [0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d=0.2:c1=tri:c2=tri[a]
how_hyperframes: hyperframes-audio crossfade between the two audio clips at the cut.
purpose: Link scenes in meaning; smooth scene change.
avoid_when: dialogue clarity is needed
breaks_continuity_when: the two sounds don't resemble each other - feels like an audio error.
common_mistakes: level jump at the crossfade
check: Loudness stays within ~3 LU across the bridge.

name: Dissolve (cross-dissolve)
definition: A fades out while B fades in, overlapping.
how: 0.5-1.5 s; both images visible mid-way, so compose them to look good superimposed.
how_html: rig.js: R.dissolve(t, 0.8-1.2).
how_ffmpeg: [0:v][1:v]xfade=transition=fade:duration=0.8:offset=<durA-0.8>[v] (also transition=dissolve for a dithered look); audio acrossfade=d=0.8.
how_hyperframes: Registry 'crossfade' (default 0.5 s) or 'blur-crossfade' (calm, 0.6 s).
purpose: Time passes a little; soft link between related moments.
avoid_when: fast promos (feels slow/dated)
within a continuous-time dialogue (implies time skipped)
breaks_continuity_when: used inside continuous action - viewer reads a time jump that didn't happen.
common_mistakes: mid-dissolve frame is a muddy mess of two busy images
check: Export the mid frame: is it readable or at least pretty?

name: Fade / dip to black
definition: Fade A to black, then B up from black.
how: 1-1.6 s total; can hold black 6-12 frames for a chapter break.
how_html: rig.js: R.dip(t, 1-1.6).
how_ffmpeg: xfade=transition=fadeblack:duration=1.2:offset=<...>
how_hyperframes: Fade the outgoing clip to black on the final scene; mid-composition use a black solid clip with opacity tweens.
purpose: End of chapter, night falls, death, time gap.
avoid_when: first 3 s of a short video (a black frame invites a swipe)
breaks_continuity_when: by design.
common_mistakes: black thumbnail frame on social platforms
check: First frame and cover frame are not black.

name: Dip to white / flash
definition: Fade or flash to white between shots.
how: Flash: 2-4 frames full white; dip: 0.4-1 s.
how_html: rig.js: R.dip(t, 0.6, '#fff').
how_ffmpeg: xfade=transition=fadewhite:duration=0.6:offset=<...>
how_hyperframes: Overexposure transition (filter: brightness()) per HyperFrames transition catalog.
purpose: Memory, flashback, camera flash, revelation, heaven.
avoid_when: viewers sensitive to flashes - avoid repeated full-screen flashes (photosensitivity)
breaks_continuity_when: by design.
common_mistakes: repeated strobing flashes
check: No more than 3 full-screen flashes in any one second.

name: Wipe / push / slide
definition: B replaces A behind a moving edge (wipe) or pushes A off-screen (push/slide).
how: Direction should follow screen direction of the story (forward = left-to-right for LTR readers).
how_html: X.wipe(sel, t, 0.6, 'left') in fx.js; CSS clip-path inset() tween.
how_ffmpeg: xfade=transition=wipeleft (or slideleft, smoothleft, circleopen, radial):duration=0.5:offset=<...>
how_hyperframes: Registry push/slide transitions ('push slide' medium energy, 0.3-0.5 s, power2/power3).
purpose: Change of place/topic; storybook or editorial feel; 'next point' in explainers.
avoid_when: serious drama (draws attention to itself)
breaks_continuity_when: wipe direction contradicts motion direction in the shots.
common_mistakes: a different wipe for every scene - HyperFrames guide: pick one primary + 1-2 accents
check: One transition family dominates (60-70% of scene changes).

name: Iris in/out
definition: A circular mask closes on (or opens from) a point.
how: Centre the iris on the face/object; hold a beat when closed.
how_html: fx.js: X.iris(sel, t, 1, x, y, 'out').
how_ffmpeg: xfade=transition=circleclose (or circleopen):duration=1:offset=<...>
how_hyperframes: 'circle iris' accent (calm) in the transition overview.
purpose: Cartoon ending, spotlight a detail, silent-film homage.
avoid_when: realistic drama
breaks_continuity_when: by design.
common_mistakes: iris centre not on the subject
check: Last visible point is the subject's face.

name: Whip pan transition
definition: Very fast pan with motion blur; cut hidden in the blur joins two shots.
how: End A with a fast pan, start B mid-pan in the same direction; cut inside the blur.
how_html: Translate layer A by -100% with blur(20px) over 0.12 s, B enters from +100% with blur over 0.12 s; same direction.
how_ffmpeg: Add directional blur: [a]...,tblend or boxblur over the last 4 frames; xfade=transition=slideleft:duration=0.2 or hblur.
how_hyperframes: Shader 'whip pan' (medium energy) per transition overview.
purpose: Energy, 'meanwhile', link two places quickly.
avoid_when: calm content; viewers prone to motion sickness
breaks_continuity_when: directions of the two pans differ.

examples.note: whip pan between characters produced uncoordinated gaze and optokinetic eye movements; Smith links this to a seasick feeling

ai_video_prompt: End of A: 'camera whip pans quickly to the right, heavy motion blur'. Start of B: 'camera whip pan from the left settles on the shop front'.
common_mistakes: blur too weak - the cut becomes visible
check: Frames around the cut are unreadable blur of the same direction.

name: Hidden cut (wipe-by / object pass)
definition: Something fills the frame (a passing person, a dark doorframe, the camera pushing into a black surface); cut while the frame is filled to fake a long take.
how: End A when the occluder covers 100% of frame; start B with an occluder leaving in the same direction.
how_html: Animate a foreground occluder layer across the frame; R.cut(t) when it covers fully.
how_ffmpeg: Concat at the full-occlusion frame; optional xfade=fade:duration=0.08 to smooth.
how_hyperframes: Foreground occluder element on top track; clip swap under it.
purpose: Simulate a continuous shot; transform location seamlessly.
avoid_when: occluder looks unmotivated
breaks_continuity_when: occluder does not fully cover, or its motion direction changes.

examples.note: continuous background and movement hide a change (substitution), cited by Smith

ai_video_prompt: 'a person walks right-to-left very close to the camera, filling the frame'.
common_mistakes: partial cover
check: Full-frame cover for at least 1-2 frames.

name: Zoom-through / push-through
definition: Camera rushes into an element (lens, window, eye) that becomes the next scene.
how: Scale A up 1->4 with blur toward a target point; B starts scaled from 0.6->1 centred on the same point.
how_html: GSAP: tl.to('#A',{scale:4,filter:'blur(10px)',transformOrigin:'x% y%',duration:.25,ease:'power4.in'},t); tl.fromTo('#B',{scale:.6,opacity:0},{scale:1,opacity:1,duration:.3,ease:'power4.out'},t+.2);
how_ffmpeg: xfade=transition=zoomin:duration=0.4:offset=<...> (centre only); for an off-centre point pre-crop/scale with zoompan.
how_hyperframes: 'Zoom through' (high energy, 0.15-0.3 s) in transition overview.
purpose: Enter a world/detail; high-energy promo transition.
use_when: going 'into' the lens of glasses, a phone screen, an eye
avoid_when: calm or serious tone
breaks_continuity_when: target point not aligned between A and B.
ai_image_prompt: B framed so the entry point is where the lens was in A.
ai_video_prompt: 'fast push-in through the lens of the glasses into a sunny beach scene'.
common_mistakes: AI video zooms produce warped geometry - build in compositing instead
check: Target point stays fixed on screen through the transition.

name: Morph / AI morph transition
definition: One image continuously transforms into another (shape interpolation or AI first-last-frame video).
how: Generate a short video with first frame = end of A and last frame = start of B (models that support first/last frame), or use a dissolve + warp.
how_html: SVG path morph (hyperframes-keyframes covers SVG morph) for flat graphics.
how_ffmpeg: Approximation only: xfade=transition=distance or fade with minterpolate; true morph needs a model.
how_hyperframes: SVG morph for vector shapes; shader 'cross-warp morph' (calm) in the transition overview.
purpose: Transformation as story (sketch becomes product, child becomes adult).
avoid_when: identity must stay exact (product shape drifts in AI morphs)
breaks_continuity_when: intermediate frames show a deformed product or face.
ai_video_prompt: First-last-frame: 'smooth continuous transformation, static camera, no new objects appear'. Check the model's docs - capability changes over time; Wan 2.2 TI2V in our CAPABILITY_MATRIX is verified for single-image start only.
common_mistakes: using it for decoration
check: Step through every 3rd frame for deformation.

name: Glitch cut
definition: Digital corruption (RGB split, slice displacement, noise) across the cut.
how: 4-8 frames of glitch centred on the cut; pair with a digital SFX.
how_html: fx.js: X.glitch across the cut.
how_ffmpeg: xfade=transition=pixelize (or hlslice):duration=0.2; add rgbashift=rh=-8:bh=8 on the boundary frames.
how_hyperframes: Registry/search 'glitch' / 'chromatic split' (hyperframes-registry).
purpose: Digital/tech feel, disorientation, 'reality breaking'.
avoid_when: calm, trust, premium brand
breaks_continuity_when: by design.
common_mistakes: overuse
flashing patterns (photosensitivity)
check: Under 3 flashes per second.

name: Freeze frame
definition: Action stops on one frame (often with a caption/name or a comic beat).
how: Freeze on the most expressive frame; 0.6-2 s; can add a record-scratch or caption.
how_html: Pause the puppet timeline (tl.pause tween) while overlay text animates.
how_ffmpeg: tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=1 on a trimmed segment, then concat.
how_hyperframes: Hold the clip's final frame (extend data-duration of an image of that frame) with overlay.
purpose: Introduce a character, punctuate a joke, end on a question.
avoid_when: mid-action where motion matters
breaks_continuity_when: by design.
common_mistakes: freezing on a blink or blur frame
check: Frozen frame is sharp, eyes open.

name: Accelerating cutting (montage build)
definition: Successive shots get shorter toward a climax, often with increasing motion.
how: Example run: 2.0, 1.6, 1.2, 0.9, 0.6, 0.4 s, then a long held shot as release.
how_html: Generate cut times from a decreasing series; align to music beats (librosa-beats).
how_ffmpeg: Script a concat list with decreasing durations.
how_hyperframes: Beat-synced clip schedule (music-to-video / beat-clip pipeline).
purpose: Build arousal toward a peak.
use_when: start of a climax; product reveal build-up
avoid_when: the whole clip (no contrast)
breaks_continuity_when: shots become too short to read (< ~0.3 s for new information).

examples.note: shot durations shorten and motion increases in the first part of the climax, then lengthen with less motion at the very end

common_mistakes: no long shot after the build (no release)
check: Plot shot lengths: a falling curve followed by one long shot.

name: Audio hit on cut
definition: A percussive sound (beat, impact, whoosh end) coincides with the picture cut.
how: Place the transient on the first frame of B (or 1 frame before).
how_html: Schedule SFX at t (sfxlib).
how_ffmpeg: [sfx]adelay=t_ms|t_ms[s]; amix with main audio.
how_hyperframes: SFX clip data-start = cut time; hyperframes-audio for level.
purpose: Make a cut feel intentional and rhythmic.
avoid_when: every cut in a calm piece
common_mistakes: hit late by 2-3 frames (feels sloppy)
check: Waveform transient aligned within 1 frame of the cut.

name: Whoosh under a transition
definition: A rising/falling air sound that matches a movement transition (whip, push, zoom).
how: Peak of the whoosh at the cut point; length equals transition length.
how_html: Schedule SFX starting at t - dur/2.
how_ffmpeg: adelay to (t - dur/2); amix.
how_hyperframes: SFX from media-use / sfxlib aligned to the transition start.
purpose: Sell the motion of the transition.
avoid_when: dialogue scenes
common_mistakes: same whoosh sample on every transition
check: Vary 2-3 samples; peaks aligned.
